Pro-Life

Constitution candidate for Governor, Idaho · Challenger

Organic strawberry farmer

Pro-Life, legally named Marvin Thomas Richardson until he changed his name, is an organic strawberry farmer from Letha, Idaho, and is on the 2026 ballot for governor as the Constitution Party nominee. He has run for Idaho offices many times since 2004, including governor in 2006, U.S. House in 2020, and lieutenant governor in 2022, when he received 5.1% of the vote. Idaho ballots list him as "Pro-Life (a person formerly known as Marvin Richardson)."

Where Pro-Life stands

Abortion
Opposes abortion. He legally changed his name to "Pro-Life" because of this position, and his campaign website lists opposing abortion as a key issue.
Central banking
Opposes central banks, which his campaign website lists as a key issue.
Approach to public service
Says public officials "should serve their fellowmen for the sake of love and eternal accountability" rather than for personal gain.

Background

  • Born Marvin Thomas Richardson, August 5, 1941, Carbon County, Wyoming
  • B.A., political science, Brigham Young University (1967)
  • Organic farmer (mainly strawberries) since 2002; previously an accountant, coal miner, and salesman of irrigation equipment and Caterpillar parts
  • Candidate, Idaho House of Representatives (2004)
  • Candidate for governor of Idaho (2006), listed on the ballot as Marvin Richardson
  • Independent candidate, U.S. Senate (2008)
  • Candidate, U.S. House (2020), 2.2% of the vote
  • Constitution Party nominee for lieutenant governor of Idaho (2022), 5.1% of the vote
  • Constitution Party nominee for governor of Idaho (2026)
